proof_findings.reason: The exact error decomposition compares clearly specified contract/model/grid targets; price-to-IV bound requires both roots inside an interval with a positive vega lower bound. Central gamma evaluation-error coefficient is 4/h^2, distinct from truncation and model error.

Initial delta shares adjusted by exp(-q dt) grow to the required next-date shares under reinvestment; the resulting p uses r-q and is strictly interior. Finite Snell induction both dominates every feasible stopping rule and constructs one attaining the maximum. Nested dates are ordered only under the same law and information. Independent full-history policy enumeration confirms prices without assuming recombination restricts admissible decisions.

Discounting removes the zeroth-order reaction and log coordinates give a=sigma^2/2, b=r-q-a. The left/right drift signs are correct. Spatial nonnegativity and explicit time restrictions are independent; positive row weights sum to one. Initial and every boundary date enter the maximum principle. Negative-rate conversion multiplies errors by exp(-rT).

Taylor/integral remainders yield k Mtt/2, a h^2 M4/12 and abs(b) h^2 M3/6. The stable recurrence gives epsilon+T eta on a closed rectangle with the stated smooth derivatives. Vanilla initial kink violates those hypotheses; the text explicitly declines to import the smooth rate to raw put values. Manufactured derivative suprema and errors verified by an independent sine spectral solution of the discrete operator.

Exact vanilla boundary arrays are identified as a verification device; the maximum boundary discrepancy only bounds the difference between the two discrete schemes. Domain enlargement at fixed node count coarsens space and changes error/stability. Strict diagonal dominance gives nonsingularity and a negative-minimum contradiction gives positivity for the stated implicit operator; no universal Crank-Nicolson positivity claim is made.

proof_findings.reason: IID finite second moments support mean/variance and fixed-n CLT with positive population variance; zero sample variance in rare events is not certification. Tilted bounded variance proves the stated two-sided Hoeffding inequality. Exact terminal GBM removes terminal-law discretization but not unobserved barriers. SHA256/Box-Muller protocol is reproducible and explicitly distinguished from proved ideal IID normals.

Square-integrability precedes covariance identities; opposite monotonicity gives a nonpositive product, including equality. Pair means are the independent units. The square-normal counterexample and completed-square signed control optimum are correct. Independent pilot conditioning requires integrability and does not transfer to same-sample fitting. Separate adaptive integrals confirm that the baseline raw control worsens ideal paired variance, beyond the observed finite-seed example.

Gaussian square completion produces L_j and the expanded put/stock products with correct discounts. A nonzero stock control is not bounded, so the put Hoeffding bound is withheld. A frozen adapted rule has conditional expected payoff below the finite-grid supremum; individual sample means may exceed it. Evaluation reuse invalidates the simple selected-policy argument. No regression consistency or continuous-exercise convergence is claimed.
